sentences.text: This miscellaneous first appeal is filed by petitioner under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'the Act'), seeking enhancement of compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicles accident dated 09.07.2012.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

3. It is the case of the petitioner that on 09.07.2012 at about 8:40 a.m. the injured was proceeding towards Kolar industry on his own bicycle on Bidar Chidri, at that time in the opposite direction a mind van bearing Reg.No.KA-32-N-1826 came in a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner lost the control and dashed to injured-petitioner.
In the said accident, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries resulting in permanent partial disability.
Inspite of prolonged treatment, he is not completely cured.
As owner and insurer, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. Respondent No.1 appeared but not filed written statement.

Respondent No.2 has appeared and filed separate written statement disputing the age, occupation, income of the petitioner, nature of injuries sustained by him and that they have resulted in permanent partial disability and also medical expenses incurred for the treatment.

As the driver of the offending vehicle had no driving licence therefore, there is violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy,
respondent/insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
5. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
6. Petitioner got himself examined as P.W.1 and relied upon Exs.P.1 to 8.
Respondents have not led any evidence on their behalf.

7. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by the petitioner granting compensation in a sum of Rs.66,500/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same as detailed below:
Sl. Nature of the heads Compensation No.
1. Pain & sufferings Rs.30,000/-
2. Medical Expenses Rs.5,000/-
Vilasrao S/O Vasudevrao vs Dhanaraj And Anr on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3259776/
2

3. Towards conveyance and Rs.31,500/-
nourishment Total Rs.66,500/-
8.
Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.

9. During the course of arguments, learned counsel representing the petitioner submitted that the Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards loss of amenities, loss of income during laid up period, attendant charges, future earnings, future medical expenses etc.

Hence, sought for allowing the appeal.
10.
On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent/insurance company supported the impugned judgment and award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

11. Heard arguments and perused the records.
12.
It is seen that the owner/insurer had not challenged the judgment and award and therefore accepted the liability to pay the compensation.
Insofar as claim for compensation is concerned

,
injuries show that claimant had suffered permanent disability.

Considering the nature of injuries,
period of treatment, medical bills, I am of the considered opinion that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be re- determined and re-calculated as under:-
Sl. Heads Amount awarded Amount awarded No by the Tribunal by this Court 1. Pain & sufferings Rs.30,000/- Rs.30,000/-
2. Medical Expenses Rs.5,000/- Rs.5,000/-
3. Towards conveyance Rs.31,500/- Rs.31,500/-
and nourishment 4. Loss of amenities ---- Rs.30,000/-
5. Loss of income ---- Rs.5,000/-
during laid up period 6.

Loss of amenities ---- Rs.5,000/-
Total Rs.66,500/- Rs.1,06,500/-
13.

To this extent, the appeal deserves to be modified and Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
Vilasrao S/O Vasudevrao vs Dhanaraj And Anr on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3259776/
3 ORDER

entities.text: Vilasrao S/O Vasudevrao vs Dhanaraj And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (i) The Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The appellant is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.1,06,500/- as against Rs.66,500/-
granted by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
(iii) Respondent/Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount together with interest at 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.
(iv) Vide order dated 26.09.2022 the petitioner- claimant is not entitled to any interest on the enhanced compensation for the delayed period.
(v) Registry is directed to send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.
Sd/-
